The advance helper is not cumulative: the final advance(1, ...) is compared against the full min_show_time/min_delay (1 >= 650 is false), so the helper never flips the state and the object is never told that time passed.

The advance helper is not cumulative: the final advance(1, ...) is compared against the full min_show_time/min_delay (1 >= 500 is false), so the helper never flips the state and the object is never told that time passed.

The helper only flips private flags and never advances a clock the object can see, so when hide() is called, the object is in the same state as in the companion 'before min show time' / animated-hide tests, which expect it to stay visible (e.g. test_hide_with_animation_hides_with_fade_public; DelayedProgressBar.java:135-145). Both can't pass; this oracle passes the ones that match Java's diff < minShowTime branch.
